newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - BTPs to get another chance at 134.84.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - BTPs to get another chance at 134.84.

text.p: September BTP futures on LIFFE may have enough gumption to break new ground above the all-time high at 134.84 on Tuesday, technical analysts said.
But failure to take advantage of the initial push higher would lead to a long-awaited correction.
"We're bouncing a bit this morning," said Elizabeth Miller, technical analyst at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell in London.
BTPs were quoted at 134.04 at 0725 GMT, up four basis points from Monday.
She said the contract faced immediate resistance at 134.30, a small high on 30 minute charts from Monday.
"Once we get back through there we should see the range highs tested again but by the end of the day we think it's going to come off again," Miller said. "It's very choppy behaviour at the moment."
The major upside objective was the high of 134.84 hit on June 26. Above there, an Elliott Wave fifth wave extension gave a target of 135.09, Miller said.
To the downside, initial support would come in at 133.75,70. Daily charts show the bottom of the past week's trading range at 133.75 on June 27. The peak of the range before was at 133.70 on June 19.
Below there, support comes in at 133.37 and a stronger buttress at 132.46, Miller said. The latter level was a 38.2 percent retracement of the gains from the May 30 low at 128.60.
Gerry Celaya, senior technical analyst at American Express Bank in London, said the contract was preparing for a correction after stalling at the 134.84, 135.00 area.
He expected BTPs to break through congestion at 133.80,70 for a move to the low 133.00s and the 132.55 June 19 low. "It's pretty bearish," he said.
September Eurolire were quoted at 93.46, down 0.02 on the day.
